items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: they sent Frank Buck over at one of our short intermissions... So Frank Buck came, however, with a pith helmet and all his array... with an ape, or a monkey, as you will.

ctx.x: Another incident you might enjoy, Milt Hinton, I don't know whether you can use it in our biography -- however, while we were at the Pennsylvania Roof, that summer of 1939, we doubled for a couple of weeks at the World's Fair, that was the beginning, the 1939-1940 World's Fair in Flushing Meadows, and we doubled afternoons. They had a band show there, and the people would roam around and then come up to hear the bands of the era, and we were there for two weeks.

And while we were there, a set up of that band shell was across from the Frank Buck display; he was there, he was alive then, with some animals. And we had in the band a wonderful trumpet player, whom I know you worked with, just

a great lead trumpet player. He was with Tommy's band, his name was Andy Peretti, he was well known for his griping, he was an artist at griping, and he was also very beloved by all musicians as a great artist, and they sent Frank Buck over at one of our short intermissions; we were still sitting on the Bandstand, and he came over to get the crowds around and they used to advertise; they'd take times like this to advertise because they had a big crowd listening to our band.
